properties.description:
PROPOSAL 1, built 2026-08-20 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM the two nodes nearest it: one was a single re-placement of reflow2's own kernel, the other measures whether walls hold. This is the OPERATION a user of any project needs to do either.

THE GAP, found by using reflow2 and MEASURED the way a user would hit it. Asked in a user's own words — "move a component to a different parent, re-decompose" — find_tools ranked contain_component top of 152 served tools. contain_component ADDS a parent and removes nothing, so the discoverable route is also the wrong one: the spine stops being a tree, and hierarchy_issues reports multiple_parents AFTERWARDS, which is the wrong end of the act. Re-decomposition is not exotic — adopting a brownfield system, acting on a design review, and severability work all consist of it.

VERIFIED THE SAME WAY THE GAP WAS MEASURED: the identical query now ranks move_component first of 153, scoring 67.5 against add_component's 44.9.

WHAT IT DOES: move_component(child_id, new_parent_id) detaches EVERY parent the child had and names them.
  · It detaches a Project parent too. A component with no subsystem is often wired straight to the project PRECISELY BECAUSE it is homeless, so a move that only looked for Component parents would create the very defect it exists to prevent. That is not hypothetical - it happened to cmp:identity the same day.
  · An EMPTY detached list is reported rather than folded into success: "placed for the first time" and "moved" are different facts, and a caller who believed they were moving something learns they were not.
  · The level relation is REPORTED in level_note, never enforced - hierarchy_issues is the authority, and one rule with two homes is one rule that can disagree with itself. But it fires AT THE MOMENT OF THE MOVE, which is the difference between a defect avoided and a defect found.
  · It does not snapshot for the caller - choosing the epoch is their call - but history_note names the record_change that preserves the previous parent whenever anything was detached.

FIRST USE ON A REAL DESIGN, not a fixture: cmp:skills had carried two parents since before this session. One call detached the stale proj:reflow2 containment; hierarchy_issues went 3 findings to 2.

A BUG FOUND BY USING IT, fixed before it shipped: history_note originally stayed silent whenever the child had ANY snapshot. A snapshot from an earlier epoch is no evidence that THIS move was recorded, so the rule went quiet for exactly the long-lived node whose history matters most - silent in the dangerous direction. It now fires on any detachment and states a fact rather than making an accusation. an_earlier_snapshot_does_not_silence_the_history_note pins it.

STATED LIMIT: this fixes the CONTAINMENT spine only. DEPENDS_ON, PROVIDES and CONSUMES edges follow the component unchanged, so a move can put a contract across a wall it did not previously cross and nothing says so.
properties.name: A component can be MOVED on the decomposition spine, not merely given another parent
